jobs.title: Director, Data Governance
jobs.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

About The Role

McKesson is seeking a strategic and experienced Director, Data Governance to lead enterprise-wide data governance programs that improve data quality, regulatory compliance, business trust, and operational excellence. This leader will define and execute governance strategies across data governance, metadata management, data cataloging, data quality, master data management, and data lineage capabilities.

The Director will partner with business, technology, risk, compliance, and data leaders to establish governance frameworks, standards, policies, and controls that support data-driven decision making and regulatory requirements. This role requires a strong combination of leadership, stakeholder engagement, data management expertise, and the ability to influence outcomes across a complex enterprise environment.

What You'll Do

Lead enterprise data governance strategy, operating model, policies, standards, and controls.
Drive adoption and optimization of data governance and data catalog platforms.
Establish and oversee data quality, metadata management, master data, and data lineage programs.
Partner with Risk, Compliance, Privacy, Security, and Audit teams to ensure regulatory compliance and governance readiness.
Develop governance metrics, data health KPIs, and executive reporting for senior leadership.
Engage business stakeholders to define data ownership, stewardship, accountability, and governance priorities.
Lead cross-functional teams delivering large-scale governance and data management initiatives.
Build and develop high-performing teams while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Basic Requirements

12+ years of professional experience in data governance, data management, data architecture, analytics, compliance, or related disciplines, including 4+ years of people leadership experience.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience.
Experience leading enterprise-scale data governance programs and operating models.
Experience implementing or managing data catalog, metadata management, or governance platforms.
Experience with data quality management, data lineage, data stewardship, and governance controls.
Experience partnering with compliance, risk, privacy, audit, or regulatory organizations.
Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and influence senior stakeholders.
Experience defining governance policies, standards, KPIs, and reporting frameworks.

Preferred Skills/Experience

Master's degree in Information Management, Computer Science, Business, Data Analytics, or a related field.
Experience supporting regulated industries such as healthcare, pharmaceutical, financial services, or insurance.
Knowledge of data governance platforms such as Collibra, Alation, Informatica, Microsoft Purview, or similar tools.
Experience with DAMA-DMBOK principles and enterprise data management frameworks.
Knowledge of data privacy regulations, governance controls, and risk management frameworks.
Experience leading enterprise-wide data transformation initiatives.
Strong executive communication and organizational change management capabilities.
Relevant certifications related to data governance, data management, privacy, or cloud technologies.

Travel, Work Environment & Physical Requirements

Ability to travel up to 20% as business needs require.
Hybrid or remote work arrangements may be available based on business and geographic requirements.
Ability to participate in virtual and in-person meetings and work effectively in a technology-enabled environment.

For McKesson Canada:
Employees are required to be in the office two (2) days per week
, either in Ville Saint-Laurent, Quebec or Mississauga, Ontario.

We are proud to offer a competitive compensation package at McKesson as part of our Total Rewards. This is determined by several factors, including performance, experience and skills, equity, regular job market evaluations, and geographical markets. In addition to base pay, other compensation, such as an annual bonus or long-term incentive opportunities may be offered. For more information regarding benefits at McKesson, please click here.

Chez nous, la santé, le bonheur et le bien-être de nos gens et des personnes que nous desservons sont prioritaires—et nous tiennent à cœur.

Ce que tu fais chez McKesson a de l’importance. Nous favorisons une culture où tu peux t’épanouir et avoir un impact, et où tu es encouragé à proposer de nouvelles idées. Ensemble, nous façonnons l’avenir de la santé pour nos patients, nos communautés et nos équipes. Si tu souhaites dès aujourd’hui contribuer à la santé de demain, nous aimerions avoir de tes nouvelles.

McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

À propos du poste

McKesson
est à la recherche d’un(e) Directeur(trice), Gouvernance des données
stratégique et expérimenté(e) pour diriger les programmes de gouvernance des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise afin d’améliorer la qualité des données, la conformité réglementaire, la confiance des parties prenantes et l’excellence opérationnelle. Cette personne définira et mettra en œuvre des stratégies de gouvernance couvrant la gouvernance des données, la gestion des métadonnées, le catalogage des données, la qualité des données, la gestion des données maîtres (MDM) et les capacités de traçabilité des données (data lineage).

Le ou la titulaire collaborera étroitement avec les équipes d’affaires, technologiques, de gestion des risques, de conformité et de données afin d’établir des cadres de gouvernance, des normes, des politiques et des contrôles soutenant la prise de décisions fondée sur les données et le respect des exigences réglementaires. Ce rôle requiert une solide combinaison de leadership, d’influence, d’expertise en gestion des données et d’engagement des parties prenantes au sein d’un environnement organisationnel complexe.

Ce que vous ferez

Diriger la stratégie de gouvernance des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise, y compris le modèle opérationnel, les politiques, les normes et les mécanismes de contrôle.
Favoriser l’adoption et l’optimisation des plateformes de gouvernance et de catalogage des données.
Établir et superviser les programmes de qualité des données, de gestion des métadonnées, de gestion des données maîtres et de traçabilité des données.
Collaborer avec les équipes des Risques, de la Conformité, de la Protection de la vie privée, de la Sécurité et de l’Audit afin d’assurer la conformité réglementaire et la maturité des pratiques de gouvernance.
Développer des indicateurs de gouvernance, des KPI de santé des données et des rapports destinés à la haute direction.
Travailler avec les parties prenantes de l’entreprise pour définir la propriété des données, l’intendance (data stewardship), la reddition de comptes et les priorités de gouvernance.
Diriger des équipes multidisciplinaires responsables d’initiatives d’envergure en gouvernance et en gestion des données.
Recruter, développer et mobiliser des équipes performantes en favorisant une culture de responsabilité, de collaboration et d’amélioration continue.

Exigences de base

Plus de 12 ans d’expérience professionnelle en gouvernance des données, gestion des données, architecture des données, analytique, conformité ou dans un domaine connexe, dont au moins 4 ans d’expérience en gestion d’équipes.
Baccalauréat ou expérience professionnelle équivalente.
Expérience dans la direction de programmes et de modèles opérationnels de gouvernance des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise.
Expérience dans l’implantation ou la gestion de plateformes de catalogage, de gestion des métadonnées ou de gouvernance des données.
Expérience en gestion de la qualité des données, traçabilité des données, intendance des données et contrôles de gouvernance.
Expérience de collaboration avec des équipes de conformité, de gestion des risques, de protection de la vie privée, d’audit ou de réglementation.
Capacité démontrée à diriger des initiatives transversales et à influencer des parties prenantes de haut niveau.
Expérience dans l’élaboration de politiques, de normes, de KPI et de cadres de reddition de comptes en matière de gouvernance.

Compétences et expérience privilégiées

Maîtrise en gestion de l’information, informatique, administration des affaires, analytique des données ou dans un domaine connexe.
Expérience dans des secteurs réglementés tels que les soins de santé, les produits pharmaceutiques, les services financiers ou l’assurance.
Connaissance de plateformes de gouvernance des données telles que Collibra, Alation, Informatica, Microsoft Purview ou des outils similaires.
Expérience avec les principes DAMA-DMBOK et les cadres de gestion des données d’entreprise.
Connaissance des règlements en matière de protection des données, des mécanismes de gouvernance et des cadres de gestion des risques.
Expérience à diriger des initiatives de transformation des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise.
Excellentes compétences en communication auprès des dirigeants et en gestion du changement organisationnel.
Certifications pertinentes en gouvernance des données, gestion des données, protection de la vie privée ou technologies infonuagiques.

Déplacements, environnement de travail et exigences physiques

Capacité à voyager jusqu’à 20 % du temps, selon les besoins de l’entreprise.
Modalités de travail hybrides ou à distance pouvant être offertes selon les besoins de l’entreprise et la situation géographique.
Capacité à participer à des réunions virtuelles et en personne et à travailler efficacement dans un environnement soutenu par la technologie.

jobs.title: Director, Global Fraud Technology - Service Reliability & Production Engineering
jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 264923

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

The Team

The Global Fraud Technology team develops and manages enterprise fraud capabilities that protect Scotiabank, its customers, and its employees across all channels and products. The Fraud Technology Service Reliability & Production Engineering organization is responsible for ensuring the reliability, stability, availability, and operational excellence of the Bank’s fraud technology ecosystem.

We partner closely with Fraud Operations, Fraud Strategy, Enterprise Operations, Infrastructure Services, Cyber Security, Payments Technology, Digital Banking, Canadian Banking, International Banking and Enterprise Technology teams to provide 24×7 operational support, incident management, service reliability, platform monitoring, production governance, and operational readiness across fraud technology platforms.

Our mission is to ensure fraud technology capabilities remain resilient, secure, highly available, and capable of supporting the Bank’s global operations and customer protection objectives.

The Role

The Director, Global Fraud Technology – Service Reliability & Production Engineering is accountable for the operational stability, reliability, and production support of the Bank’s fraud technology portfolio. This role leads a team of 25+ professionals — spanning FTE and managed services partners across Toronto, Bogotá, Bangalore, and Chennai — responsible for application support, production operations, site reliability engineering, observability, incident management, problem management, operational governance, environment management, release readiness, and service continuity.

The Director provides direct leadership to Senior Managers responsible for Fraud Production Engineering and Observability / Logging & Monitoring functions, and has strategic oversight of managed services partnerships, including vendor SLA governance, and operational delivery standards.

The Director is responsible for establishing operational excellence practices that ensure fraud technology services consistently meet availability, performance, resilience, and supportability objectives while minimizing operational risk. This includes driving the expansion of operational support coverage from current markets (Canada, Caribbean) to global fraud technology platforms across International Banking (Mexico, Peru, Chile and Uruguay)

The role works closely with technology, infrastructure, security, and business leaders to ensure production environments operate effectively and that operational risks are proactively identified and mitigated.

Key Accountabilities

Strategy & Leadership

Develop and execute the multi-year Fraud Technology Operations strategy aligned with enterprise technology and fraud objectives, including the roadmap for expanding operational support from Canada and the Caribbean to all International Banking markets.
Establish operational excellence frameworks, support models, reliability targets, and service management standards across the fraud technology portfolio.
Define the future-state operating model for production support, service reliability, observability, and operational governance.
Partner with business and technology stakeholders to improve service quality, resilience, and operational effectiveness.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on automation, operational maturity, and service reliability.
Lead strategic vendor relationships supporting operational and monitoring capabilities.

Production Support Leadership

Lead global support teams responsible for fraud technology platforms operating across multiple geographies and time zones.
Establish support processes that ensure timely investigation, resolution, escalation, and communication of production issues
Ensure critical fraud systems maintain agreed-upon availability and performance objectives.
Drive operational readiness reviews and support transitions for new projects and platform releases.
Establish strong partnerships with enterprise operations, infrastructure, and business support teams.
Drive the expansion of operational support coverage to global fraud technology platforms, defining staffing, tooling, and process requirements for new market onboarding.

Incident & Problem Management

Own major incident management processes for fraud technology services.
Lead coordinated responses to critical production incidents impacting fraud detection, fraud response, customer protection, or operational capabilities.
Establish root cause analysis and problem management disciplines to reduce recurring issues.
Drive post-incident reviews and operational improvement initiatives.
Ensure incident communications, escalation procedures, and executive reporting processes are effective and timely.

Site Reliability Engineering & Observability

Lead adoption of Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) principles across fraud technology platforms.
Establish reliability engineering practices, operational metrics, and service-level objectives.
Drive implementation of monitoring, observability, alerting, logging, and performance management capabilities.
Improve proactive detection of operational issues through automation and intelligent monitoring.
Develop operational dashboards and service health reporting for technical and business stakeholders.
Establish data pipeline and ingestion monitoring capabilities

Platform Reliability & Resilience

Ensure fraud technology services are designed and operated for high availability, resilience, and recoverability.
Establish operational controls supporting business continuity, disaster recovery, and resiliency requirements.
Partner with architecture, engineering, and infrastructure teams to improve platform reliability.
Drive capacity planning, performance optimization, and infrastructure readiness activities.
Identify operational risks and ensure mitigation strategies are implemented.

Change, Release & Environment Management

Govern operational readiness for Fraud systems and ensure enterprise change processes awareness for production releases and platform changes
Partner with engineering teams to improve deployment automation and release quality.
Reduce operational risk associated with technology changes.

Operational Risk & Governance

Ensure operational processes align with the Bank’s risk appetite, regulatory obligations, and technology governance frameworks.
Maintain effective controls supporting audit, compliance, and regulatory requirements.
Partner with Risk Management, Compliance, Audit, and Security teams to strengthen operational governance.
Ensure operational procedures, runbooks, support documentation, and recovery plans remain current and effective.
Establish measurable operational controls and service performance indicators.

Automation & Operational Efficiency

Drive automation initiatives that improve support effectiveness and reduce manual operational activities.
Implement self-healing capabilities, automated remediation processes, and intelligent operational tooling.
Improve operational productivity through standardized processes and platform automation.
Establish DataOps, DevOps, and SRE practices that improve operational efficiency and service quality.
Reduce operational toil and increase engineering productivity.

Talent Leadership

Build, lead, and develop high-performing operational support, SRE, platform engineering, and reliability teams spanning FTE and managed services resources across multiple geographies.
Foster a culture of accountability, operational excellence, continuous improvement, and customer focus.
Coach and mentor managers, senior engineers, and technical leaders.
Develop succession plans and long-term talent strategies for critical operational leadership roles.
Champion Agile, DevOps, SRE, and continuous improvement methodologies.
Manage the balance between FTE and managed services capacity to optimize cost, coverage, and capability.

General

Champions a customer-focused culture to deepen client relationships and leverage broader Bank relationships, systems, and knowledge.
Understands how the Bank’s risk appetite and risk culture should be considered in day-to-day activities and decisions.
Actively pursues effective and efficient operations in accordance with Scotiabank’s Values, Code of Conduct, and Global Sales Principles while ensuring the adequacy, adherence to, and effectiveness of business controls relating to operational, compliance, AML/ATF/sanctions, conduct, cyber, and technology risk.

What You Will Bring To Succeed

Must Have

10+ years of progressive technology leadership experience supporting enterprise applications and platforms.
5+ years of experience leading production support, application operations, SRE, infrastructure operations, or enterprise service management teams.
5+ years of leadership experience managing managers and multidisciplinary operational teams.
Deep expertise in IT Service Management (ITSM), incident management, problem management, change management, and operational governance.
Experience supporting mission-critical, high-availability platforms operating in 24×7 production environments.
Strong understanding of cloud platforms, preferably Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and Azure.
Experience implementing monitoring, observability, automation, and reliability engineering capabilities.
Experience managing operational risk, disaster recovery, business continuity, and resiliency programs.
Strong executive communication, stakeholder management, and crisis management skills.
Experience operating within highly regulated financial services environments.
Experience with Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), DevOps, DevSecOps, and platform engineering operating models.

Nice to Have

Experience supporting fraud, payments, financial crime, risk, or customer protection platforms.
Experience managing global support organizations operating across multiple regions and time zones.
Knowledge of observability platforms such as Splunk, Dynatrace, or equivalent technologies.
Understanding of regulatory operational resilience expectations and technology risk management frameworks.
Experience with data pipeline monitoring, data quality management, and fraud data ingestion ecosystems.

The Workplace

We are technology partners who help the business transform how our employees around the world work.
We have an inclusive and collaborative working environment that encourages creativity, curiosity, and celebrates success!
You’ll get to work with and learn from diverse industry leaders, who have hailed from top technology companies around the world.
We foster an environment of innovation and continuous learning.
We care about our people, allowing them to design how they work to deliver amazing results.
We offer a competitive total rewards package, including a performance bonus, company matching programs (on pension & profit sharing), and generous vacation.

Scotiabank

As Canada’s International Bank, we are a diverse and global team. We speak more than 100 languages with backgrounds from more than 120 countries. We value the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the Bank and are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. If you require accommodation (including, but not limited to, an accessible interview site, alternate format documents, ASL Interpreter, or Assistive Technology) during the recruitment and selection process, please let our Recruitment team know. If you require technical assistance, please click here. Candidates must apply directly online to be considered for this role. We thank all applicants for their interest in a career at Scotiabank; however, only those candidates who are selected for an interview will be contacted.

Is This Role Not the Exact Fit?

Sign up to stay in touch; we’ll let you know when we have new positions on the team.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Technology Risk Officer
jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 259458

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

The Role

The Senior Director, Technology Risk Officer (TRO) leads the First Line of Defense (1B) Technology Risk and Internal Control function, accountable for the design, implementation, operation, and continuous improvement of technology and cybersecurity risk management practices across the enterprise. The role ensures technology and cybersecurity risks are identified, assessed, mitigated, monitored, and reported in alignment with the firm’s risk appetite, regulatory expectations, and business strategy.

This role requires a visionary leader with a deep understanding of cybersecurity principles, risk management, and compliance frameworks. The ideal candidate will possess strong communication and leadership skills, the ability to navigate complex regulatory landscapes, and a commitment to continuous improvement in the face of a rapidly evolving cybersecurity environment.

What will you do?

Own execution and accountability for Technology Risk Management and Internal Controls within the First Line of Defense (1B).
Provide direction and oversight to Technology 1A risk owners to strengthen their capability to identify, assess, mitigate, and monitor technology and cyber risks.
Serve as a trusted 1B Technology Risk partner to Technology, Product, and Business teams.
Lead the identification, escalation, monitoring, and measurement of technology and operational risks in alignment with firm-wide risk management programs.
Serve as a deep subject matter expert and trusted Technology 1B partner on cybersecurity, resiliency and physical security principles, practices and technologies across key domains, including, Threat and Vulnerability Management, Data Protection, Identity and Access Management, Cyber Incident Response, Cyber Threat Intelligence, Technology Resilience, Third Party Cyber Risk, Physical Security and Application Security.
Monitor technology risk KRIs and KPIs, supports review and challenge of remediation and get-to-green plans, and tracks delivery of sustainable risk reduction.
Ensures technology risk outcomes remain aligned to the firm’s risk appetite and governance expectations.
Prepare and presents technology risk insights, trends, and recommendations to senior management and governance forums.
Provide 1B risk and control advisory support, including targeted risk reviews, root cause analysis, and development of sustainable mitigation strategies.
Implements the firm’s technology risk management strategy, ensuring alignment with regulatory and industry standards.
Drives a proactive risk and control culture focused on prevention, transparency, and continuous improvement.

jobs.title: Director, Finance (Permanent, Full-time) Vancouver
jobs.description:
Ready to lead a finance transformation that directly fuels a mission changing lives across Vancouver?

The Director of Finance is a critical leadership role responsible for the integrity, accuracy, and reliability of the organization's financial operations, spanning accounting, compliance and audit, financial systems, budgeting and forecasting, and business partnership, while also driving the next phase of our finance function modernization. This role carries the full scope of the controllership combined with the people leadership, change management, and process redesign work needed to build a stronger, more efficient finance operation. This is a hands-on leadership position to run a clean, compliant, and well-controlled finance operation, while building the systems, processes, and team capability that will free the organization's finance function to focus on strategic, forward-looking work in the years ahead.

This is a permanent
, full-time
(37.5 hours per week) position
. The starting range for this position is $106,470 to $116,337 per annum.

Who We Are

Demonstrating the love of Christ, UGM feeds hope and changes lives through a faith-based continuum of care. We are a proud member of the Canadian Council of Christian Charities and have earned the Best Christian Workplace award again in 2021. We provide competitive salaries, generous vacation and sick leave, an RRSP matching program, as well as the potential for educational assistance and flexible work arrangements. In addition, our extensive benefits plan is fully employer-paid and includes extended dental and medical, as well as $4,500 per year in pooled paramedical expenses. A focus on employee resilience, support for professional development, engagement in meaningful work, and a fun and caring environment are all part of being a member of the UGM team. If you are someone who desires to learn and grow, has a passion to serve and make a difference, and connects with others with both humility and humour, then you will be a great fit at UGM.

Main Duties & Responsibilities

Financial Stewardship, Reporting, Compliance & Audit:

Own the full accounting cycle including but not limited to accounts receivable, revenue recognition, accounts payable, payments, cash management, petty cash, inventory, fund accounting, capital assets, inter-entity accounting, and financial reporting.
Maintain and strengthen internal controls, relevant policies, procedures, accounting standards, and regulations, and ensure timely month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close, including reconciliations, working papers, allocations, consolidation, and financial analysis.
Own the integrity of all financial records across all legal entities, funds, and projects.
Oversee restricted and unrestricted fund accounting to ensure accurate donor/grant fund tracking.
Provide consolidated and non-consolidated financial information, financial statements, dashboards, and management reporting on a monthly, quarterly, and annual basis for budget managers, executives, the Finance Committee, and the Board.
Lead all taxation matters and external reporting to the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), BC Housing, BC Gaming, regulators, grantors, funders, and other stakeholders.
Plan and lead the annual audit process, including working papers, schedules, auditor liaison, and resolution of findings.
Serve as the primary point of contact for auditors, funders, and regulatory bodies on financial and compliance matters.
Ensure full compliance with ASNPO, CRA charitable regulations, funder restrictions, BC Housing agreements, and other external stakeholders' requirements.
Ensure timely and accurate completion of statutory filings, grant/funder financial reporting, and other compliance requirements.
Manage multi-entity financial consolidation, ensuring consistency and accuracy across all entities.

Financial System, Data Infrastructure, Planning & Forecasting

Lead the execution of the annual budget, rolling forecast, and long-term financial planning processes across all departments and programs, in partnership with the Vice President, Finance & Operations, who sets the organization's overall financial strategy.
Develop financial models, scenario analysis, capital plans, and sensitivity analysis to support strategic investments, growth initiatives, housing projects, and funding decisions.
Provide clear financial insight on key drivers, risks, and opportunities to leadership and budget owners.
Translate the strategic direction set by the Vice President, Finance & Operations into actionable, well-structured financial plans, challenging assumptions and ensuring execution stays aligned with sustainability goals.
Serve as the power user for NetSuite, financial architecture, and data integrity — ensuring strong controls, automation, and reliable reporting — and proactively improve the ERP system's backend, leveraging updated and new technologies for continuous enhancement.

Change Management & Finance Process Redesign

Lead the execution of the finance function modernization roadmap, translating strategic priorities into concrete operational change.
Identify, prioritize, and redesign manual or inefficient accounting processes to reduce touchpoints, improve accuracy, and shorten close timelines.
Provide regular feedback to the Vice President, Finance & Operations on the progress, impact, and challenges of process changes, adjusting the approach as needed.
Lead the team through change with clear communication, structured training, and hands-on support — minimizing disruption to daily operations.
Champion a culture of continuous improvement within the finance function.

Business Partnership And Organizational Leadership

Act as a trusted partner to the Vice President, Finance & Operations, providing reliable financial information and operational insight to support organizational decision-making.
Collaborate closely with cross functional departments to ensure accurate financial and to support all departmental leaders, utilizing enhanced communication skills to build relationships and acquire necessary information and data to achieve functional goals.
Translate complex financial data into clear, actionable insights for non-financial leaders.
Support a customer-service oriented finance culture that enables mission delivery.
As the finance function matures and stabilizes, opportunity to grow into a broader strategic finance leadership role alongside the Vice President, Finance & Operations.

People & Team Leadership

Lead, coach, and develop the Finance team, including Senior Accountants, Senior Analysts, Accountants, Financial Analyst, and Financial System.
Build team capability and depth to support both current finance operations and future strategic finance work.
Set clear performance expectations, provide regular feedback, and support career development within the team.
Promote open communication and collaborative efforts within the Department and UGM as a whole, aligning with the organization's mission, core values, and strategic plan.
Lead and develop a high-performing team, fostering a culture of excellence, business partnerships, collaboration, and continuous learning.

General

Uphold financial security by following internal control procedures.
Adhere to all UGM published policies, practices, and procedures, including Occupational Health and Safety.
Perform other duties and special project as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

CPA designation or equivalent required. MBA would be an asset.
7+ years of progressive experience in finance, including significant experience within the nonprofit or charitable sector.
Strong working experience and knowledge with grant/restricted fund accounting and the deferral method.
Power-user level experience with NetSuite or another complex ERP system, with strong logical understanding of data flow and finance processes.
Experience managing multi-entity accounting and consolidation.
Proven experience planning and leading external audits from start to finish.
Strong knowledge of and experience with Not for Profit and CRA charities regulations and reporting.
Minimum 10 direct/indirect reports managed in a prior role, with demonstrated success in team leadership and development.
Strong interpersonal and written & verbal communication skills with demonstrated ability to work with cross-functional teams/departments.
Execution-focused leader who translates strategic direction into clear, actionable financial plans, with strong attention to detail.
Proficiency in English skills (reading, writing and verbal).

Working Conditions

Work Location

Work is generally performed indoors within an office environment, with standard office equipment available.

Physical Requirements

Work is generally sedentary in nature, but may require standing, walking or reaching for up to 10% of the time. Employee is required to look at a computer screen and use a keyboard for up to 90% of the time.

Work Conditions

Working environment is generally favorable. Lighting and temperature are adequate. Work is performed amid normal conditions of dust, odors, fumes, and noises. Employee is required to work with large sums of cash. Work is deadline driven. Work is cyclical and at times there will be large volumes of work to complete.

Hours of Work

Some weekend or evening work may be required. Moderate overtime may be required.

Hazards

Hazards are considered minor and controllable.

Other

Due to the nature of the job, and our commitment to a safe environment, the candidate is subject to a criminal record check.

Diriger la stratégie de gouvernance des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise, y compris le modèle opérationnel, les politiques, les normes et les mécanismes de contrôle.

Travailler avec les parties prenantes de l’entreprise pour définir la propriété des données, l’intendance (data stewardship), la reddition de comptes et les priorités de gouvernance.
Diriger des équipes multidisciplinaires responsables d’initiatives d’envergure en gouvernance et en gestion des données.
Recruter, développer et mobiliser des équipes performantes en favorisant une culture de responsabilité, de collaboration et d’amélioration continue.

Plus de 12 ans d’expérience professionnelle en gouvernance des données, gestion des données, architecture des données, analytique, conformité ou dans un domaine connexe, dont au moins 4 ans d’expérience en gestion d’équipes.
Baccalauréat ou expérience professionnelle équivalente.
Expérience dans la direction de programmes et de modèles opérationnels de gouvernance des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise.
Expérience dans l’implantation ou la gestion de plateformes de catalogage, de gestion des métadonnées ou de gouvernance des données.

Capacité démontrée à diriger des initiatives transversales et à influencer des parties prenantes de haut niveau.

Maîtrise en gestion de l’information, informatique, administration des affaires, analytique des données ou dans un domaine connexe.

In addition, our extensive benefits plan is fully employer-paid and includes extended dental and medical, as well as $4,500 per year in pooled paramedical expenses. A focus on employee resilience, support for professional development, engagement in meaningful work, and a fun and caring environment are all part of being a member of the UGM team. If you are someone who desires to learn and grow, has a passion to serve and make a difference, and connects with others with both humility and humour, then you will be a great fit at UGM.

Main Duties & Responsibilities

Financial Stewardship, Reporting, Compliance & Audit:

Own the full accounting cycle including but not limited to accounts receivable, revenue recognition, accounts payable, payments, cash management, petty cash, inventory, fund accounting, capital assets, inter-entity accounting, and financial reporting.
Maintain and strengthen internal controls, relevant policies, procedures, accounting standards, and regulations, and ensure timely month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close, including reconciliations, working papers, allocations, consolidation, and financial analysis.
Own the integrity of all financial records across all legal entities, funds, and projects.
Oversee restricted and unrestricted fund accounting to ensure accurate donor/grant fund tracking.
Provide consolidated and non-consolidated financial information, financial statements, dashboards, and management reporting on a monthly, quarterly, and annual basis for budget managers, executives, the Finance Committee, and the Board.
Lead all taxation matters and external reporting to the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), BC Housing, BC Gaming, regulators, grantors, funders, and other stakeholders.
Plan and lead the annual audit process, including working papers, schedules, auditor liaison, and resolution of findings.
Serve as the primary point of contact for auditors, funders, and regulatory bodies on financial and compliance matters.
Ensure full compliance with ASNPO, CRA charitable regulations, funder restrictions, BC Housing agreements, and other external stakeholders' requirements.
Ensure timely and accurate completion of statutory filings, grant/funder financial reporting, and other compliance requirements.
Manage multi-entity financial consolidation, ensuring consistency and accuracy across all entities.

Financial System, Data Infrastructure, Planning & Forecasting

Lead the execution of the annual budget, rolling forecast, and long-term financial planning processes across all departments and programs, in partnership with the Vice President, Finance & Operations, who sets the organization's overall financial strategy.
Develop financial models, scenario analysis, capital plans, and sensitivity analysis to support strategic investments, growth initiatives, housing projects, and funding decisions.
Provide clear financial insight on key drivers, risks, and opportunities to leadership and budget owners.
Translate the strategic direction set by the Vice President, Finance & Operations into actionable, well-structured financial plans, challenging assumptions and ensuring execution stays aligned with sustainability goals.
Serve as the power user for NetSuite, financial architecture, and data integrity — ensuring strong controls, automation, and reliable reporting — and proactively improve the ERP system's backend, leveraging updated and new technologies for continuous enhancement.

Change Management & Finance Process Redesign

Lead the execution of the finance function modernization roadmap, translating strategic priorities into concrete operational change.
Identify, prioritize, and redesign manual or inefficient accounting processes to reduce touchpoints, improve accuracy, and shorten close timelines.
Provide regular feedback to the Vice President, Finance & Operations on the progress, impact, and challenges of process changes, adjusting the approach as needed.
Lead the team through change with clear communication, structured training, and hands-on support — minimizing disruption to daily operations.
Champion a culture of continuous improvement within the finance function.

Business Partnership And Organizational Leadership

Act as a trusted partner to the Vice President, Finance & Operations, providing reliable financial information and operational insight to support organizational decision-making.
Collaborate closely with cross functional departments to ensure accurate financial and to support all departmental leaders, utilizing enhanced communication skills to build relationships and acquire necessary information and data to achieve functional goals.
Translate complex financial data into clear, actionable insights for non-financial leaders.
Support a customer-service oriented finance culture that enables mission delivery.
As the finance function matures and stabilizes, opportunity to grow into a broader strategic finance leadership role alongside the Vice President, Finance & Operations.

People & Team Leadership

Lead, coach, and develop the Finance team, including Senior Accountants, Senior Analysts, Accountants, Financial Analyst, and Financial System.
Build team capability and depth to support both current finance operations and future strategic finance work.
Set clear performance expectations, provide regular feedback, and support career development within the team.
Promote open communication and collaborative efforts within the Department and UGM as a whole, aligning with the organization's mission, core values, and strategic plan.
Lead and develop a high-performing team, fostering a culture of excellence, business partnerships, collaboration, and continuous learning.

General

Uphold financial security by following internal control procedures.
Adhere to all UGM published policies, practices, and procedures, including Occupational Health and Safety.
Perform other duties and special project as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

CPA designation or equivalent required. MBA would be an asset.
7+ years of progressive experience in finance, including significant experience within the nonprofit or charitable sector.
Strong working experience and knowledge with grant/restricted fund accounting and the deferral method.
Power-user level experience with NetSuite or another complex ERP system, with strong logical understanding of data flow and finance processes.
Experience managing multi-entity accounting and consolidation.
Proven experience planning and leading external audits from start to finish.
Strong knowledge of and experience with Not for Profit and CRA charities regulations and reporting.
Minimum 10 direct/indirect reports managed in a prior role, with demonstrated success in team leadership and development.
Strong interpersonal and written & verbal communication skills with demonstrated ability to work with cross-functional teams/departments.
Execution-focused leader who translates strategic direction into clear, actionable financial plans, with strong attention to detail.
Proficiency in English skills (reading, writing and verbal).

Working Conditions

Work Location

Work is generally performed indoors within an office environment, with standard office equipment available.

Physical Requirements

Work is generally sedentary in nature, but may require standing, walking or reaching for up to 10% of the time. Employee is required to look at a computer screen and use a keyboard for up to 90% of the time.

Work Conditions

Working environment is generally favorable. Lighting and temperature are adequate. Work is performed amid normal conditions of dust, odors, fumes, and noises. Employee is required to work with large sums of cash. Work is deadline driven. Work is cyclical and at times there will be large volumes of work to complete.

Hours of Work

Some weekend or evening work may be required. Moderate overtime may be required.

Hazards

Hazards are considered minor and controllable.

Other

Due to the nature of the job, and our commitment to a safe environment, the candidate is subject to a criminal record check.
